title: Follow-up: one argument scanner for --repo, and ADR 0002's produces nit
description: LOW from the approved review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#34 at f1942deb. The argv pre-scans in src/program.ts and commander disagree on --repo's value: `glyph --repo --json callers x` prints text on success but a JSON envelope on failure, because the pre-scan consumes --json as the option value. Fix by sharing one argument scanner between the pre-scan and option resolution. Fold in the review's NIT: ADR 0002's 'produces' sentence still omits uncaught. Filed from the #34 approval; not started.

acceptanceCriteria.text: One argument scanner identifies the command token and the --repo value identically for commander and the pre-scan; `glyph --repo --json callers x` and `glyph --repo <dir> --json callers x` choose the same output mode on a success path and a failure path.
Tests cover `--repo --json` on a success path and a failure path, and the `--repo=<dir>` form.
ADR 0002's "produces" sentence names `uncaught` beside usage, not_found and indeterminate.

plan: Add one scanArgv scanner to src/program.ts that models commander: --repo (and --repo=) takes the next token as its value even when it starts with a dash, and it identifies the first command token.
Route the pre-scan decisions, contextOf and the failure output mode through that scanner instead of a second reading of argv.
Cover --repo --json on a success path and a failure path, and --repo=<dir>; amend ADR 0002 produces sentence to name uncaught.
implementationNotes: Proof: CI run 44022396082 on 6c965f9 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check locally green, 77 tests; lore check and lore validate --strict exit 0. Mutation check: restoring the old failure-path expression (program.opts().json or argv.includes(--json)) turns only the new cli test red at its text-on-failure assertion and leaves the other 19 in that file green. The success-path text and both --repo=<dir> envelope assertions stayed green under that mutation, which is the asymmetry the fix removes.

DEC-183 round-1 reviewer verdict on opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 at head 70039a2a1f547ccf6c2684bb3126d55c4b6eac91, reviewer model claude-opus-5-5 (read-only unit, traced against commander 15.0.0; ran nothing). Recorded verbatim:

VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 at 70039a2 (GCLI-13). I traced the code against commander 15.0.0, pinned in package.json:40, in node_modules/commander/lib/command.js. I did not run anything.

Findings:

1. BLOCKING, src/program.ts:180 and :221-229. The scanner skips the token after `--file`, `--depth` and `--ref`, but commander does not. There is no enablePositionalOptions, so the program-level parseOptions runs over the whole argv first (command.js:1760-1907). At that level these three are unknown options. They switch `dest` to `unknown` at command.js:1866-1871 but do not consume the next token, so a following `--repo`, `--json` or `-v` is still taken by the program at command.js:1804-1828. Only `--repo` takes the next token at program level. Three argvs show the effect:
   a. `glyph impact x --ref --repo /dir HEAD`
      - Commander sets repo=/dir, and impact gets `--ref HEAD`. It succeeds.
      - The scanner's `--ref` eats `--repo`, so `scanned.repo` is undefined and contextOf analyzes the cwd. Result: the wrong repository, exit 0.
      - On dev, contextOf read `program.opts().repo` and analyzed /dir. This is a success-path regression, and it contradicts AC0 ("identifies … the --repo value identically for commander and the pre-scan"). The comment at :206-207 ("their value is never a command token or a flag") is wrong about commander.
   b. `glyph callers --file --json src a` (or `impact x --depth --json 3`)
      - Commander sets json=true and file=src, and succeeds.
      - The scanner sees json=false, so the output is text.
      - On dev this was a JSON envelope. Success and failure still agree with each other, but both now disagree with commander.
   c. `glyph --json impact x --depth -v`
      - The scanner's `--depth` eats `-v`, so the JSON version intercept at :458 is skipped.
      - Commander's version listener then prints the version as text to stdout under `--json`.
      - On dev, `argv.includes("-v")` produced the envelope, so this is a contract regression.
   Fix: only `--repo` should consume the next token. Drop `--file`, `--depth` and `--ref` from the skip set. They can still clear onlyKnownGlobals as unknown options, which is what commander does with them. Add a test for (a) at least. The writer's mutation check only touched the failure-path expression, so it could not catch this.

2. NIT, src/program.ts:216-239. The scanner ignores `--` (end of options). After `--`, commander moves every remaining token into operands (command.js:1789-1792), and the subcommand does not re-parse them (command.js:1563-1566). Examples:
   - `glyph callers -- --json` gets a JSON not_found envelope, but commander has json=false.
   - `glyph --json callers -- -v` gets a version envelope with exit 0, where commander would look up a symbol named `-v`.
   This predates the PR (dev's failure path also used argv.includes). Because TS identifiers and git refs cannot start with `-`, it only affects not-found or error paths in practice. Suggested fix: stop reading options at `--`, and take the first bare token after it as commandToken if none is set yet.

3. NIT, existed before this PR. Combined short flags such as `-vh` or `-hv` are unknown to the scanner. Commander splits them (command.js:1831-1848), so `glyph -vh --json` prints the version as text, with no envelope.

4. NIT, a behaviour change reported because you asked; it is not a defect. Argvs where `--repo` takes `--help`, `-h`, `--version` or `-v` as its value now count as a bare invocation:
   - `glyph --repo --help` now prints help with exit 0. On dev, wantsHelp/wantsVersion matched, the argv fell through to commander, and it failed with "(outputHelp)" as a usage error, exit 2.
   - `glyph --json --repo --version` was a version envelope on dev and is now a JSON help envelope.
   - `glyph --repo --json` was a JSON help envelope on dev and is now text help.
   All of these follow the scanner's model of `--repo` and are consistent with `glyph --repo <dir>`. Otherwise bare-invocation behaviour is unchanged: `[]`, `[--json]`, `--repo=` (empty value resolves to the cwd, same as commander), `--repo x`, `--repo` as the last token, and an unknown option all match dev.

What I verified against commander 15's source:
- These shapes agree with commander:
  - `--repo=x` and `--repo x`.
  - `--repo` as the last token: no repo, onlyKnownGlobals=false, commander raises optionMissingArgument, usage error.
  - `--repo --json`: repo is "--json" and json=false in both.
  - `--json` before or after the command: the program consumes it anywhere.
  - Repeated `--repo`: the last one wins in both.
  - `--json=x`: unknown option in both, json=false.
  - `--repo --help` and `--repo --version`: consumed as the value in both. The help option is not in this.options (command.js:2589-2611), but `--repo` is required and consumes it at :1809 anyway.
  - `-h`, `--help` and `--version` interleaved elsewhere.
- There is no short alias for `--repo` or `--json`. The only short flags are `-v` and `-h`.
- Output mode cannot differ between success and failure for the same argv: action handlers (:271/:320/:370/:401/:424), the pre-scan branches and the catch block (:490) all read `scanned.json`.
- No path writes JSON beside text: each branch emits exactly once in one mode, and a CommanderError with exitCode 0 returns without writing. The only text-under-`--json` paths are finding 1c (new) and finding 3 (older).
- The ADR 0002 change is accurate. run() emits `uncaught` at program.ts:501, and errors.ts:5 maps it to 1.
- Nothing else in program.ts changed behaviour. The diff only removes GlobalOptions, rewires contextOf, adds scanArgv, changes the buildProgram signature, and routes run() and the catch block through the scan. The contract test uses buildProgram(scanArgv([])), which is fine.
- The new cli test's assertions are consistent with the code.

What a tree read could not establish:
- I traced the code and did not execute any of it. Findings 1a-c and 2 are derived from commander's source and have not been observed running.
- I did not confirm CI run 44022396082, the 77-test count, the mutation result, or `lore check` / `lore validate --strict`.
- I did not check that node_modules in the main checkout is byte-identical to what CI installs. I read commander 15.0.0 there, matching the exact pin.

Round-1 fix (in the round-2 head). Only --repo consumes the next token now; --file, --depth and --ref are unknown at program level exactly as commander treats them, so 'impact x --ref --repo /dir HEAD' selects /dir again. Options stop at --, and the first token after it names the command if none is set. Combined short flags (-vh, -hv) are split like commander. Five new cli tests cover (a) the --repo-after-a-subcommand-option regression, (b) --json after --file, (c) -v after --depth under --json, the -- terminator both ways, and -vh; all five go red on 70039a2 before the fix and green after it. Nit 4, noted and left as the reviewer asked: a --repo that consumes --help, -h, --version or -v now counts as a bare invocation, so 'glyph --repo --help' prints help with exit 0 (dev raised a usage error), 'glyph --json --repo --version' is a JSON help envelope (dev: version envelope) and 'glyph --repo --json' is text help (dev: JSON help). All follow the scanner model of --repo and match 'glyph --repo <dir>'.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/glyph-cli#64 (commit 6c965f9): scanArgv is now the one reader of --repo, --json and the command token, following commander's own rule that --repo takes the next token as its value; contextOf, the help/version pre-parse and the failure-path output mode all take their answers from that scan, so glyph --repo --json ... speaks text on both the success and the failure path. ADR 0002 produces now names uncaught. Validated by CI run 44022396082 on 6c965f9 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity green); bun run check green, 77 tests; lore check and lore validate --strict green. Reverting the failure path to a second reading of argv turns exactly the new test red.
